Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-3-prompt-long-0064", "row_sha256": "c4c2f0ab750908f28baccef00726617f5eebbb9fe426d009d2b57fb9feebb053", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "make a prompt for a screen reader audit memo for the Harborline Library consortium site Roomline, and send the request to Idris, not Mina. this is for a short internal review, not a public statement. use the observations below as the material the writer has been given; the task is to organize them into a useful audit memo, not to claim that any extra testing happened. the site is used to search for bookable meeting rooms and make a reservation. the review covers the catalog search route and the room reservation route, including the point where a person chooses a date and time. keep those routes as the scope and don't quietly turn this into an audit of the entire library service.

the supplied test setup was Windows 11 with Firefox 134 and NVDA 2024.4, plus an iPhone SE, third generation, on iOS 18.2 with Safari and VoiceOver. the staff notes don't say that every step was repeated on both combinations, so don't imply that they were. the review material is from two staff members who tried the routes during the same week. there isn't a date for the week in the notes, and there aren't recordings or a full test script attached. include the setup as given, but don't make up dates, tester names, assistive technology settings, or a testing count beyond what is actually stated.

on the catalog search page the main heading is “Search rooms.” the search box has the accessible name “Find a room,” and the date field is marked required. after a search, the page shows a results heading and a list of available rooms. there is a filters control. in the Windows/NVDA notes, activating it opened the filter options, but the control's changed expanded state was not announced. the notes don't say whether the same thing happened with VoiceOver. a staff member wrote, “I could tell the filters had opened because the page changed, but I didn't hear the button say expanded.” keep that as a quote if the memo uses it, and don't turn the staff member's impression into a universal result. don't infer what the filter choices were, since the notes don't list them.

for the reservation route, the steps are select a date, choose a room, choose a half-hour time slot, and submit the reservation. the notes describe a progress indicator with the steps shown in order. on desktop, heading navigation moved from an H1 to an H3 in the room details area; the notes don't name an H2 or say whether one was intentionally absent. the dialog used during room selection had a close control announced as “×” in the NVDA notes. the notes don't record its accessible name on the phone. don't rewrite that observation as though the control had no name at all, and don't guess what a better name should be.

there is also an error case in the staff notes. after a person submitted without choosing a time slot, an error message appeared below the time selector. focus remained on the Save button, and the NVDA tester did not hear an announcement of the error when it appeared. the notes don't give the error's exact wording, and they don't record the VoiceOver result for that case. include the focus behavior and the missing announcement as separate observations. don't invent an error message, assume that the message was visually hidden, or say that the issue was fixed. in a successful desktop test, a confirmation panel appeared after submission. don't give the reservation a made-up name or time, and don't imply that the audit tested cancellation, email notices, or later changes to a booking.

on the phone, the notes say a sticky footer overlapped the last two time slots when the page was enlarged to 200 percent. VoiceOver swipe navigation could still reach both slots. the notes do not say whether both slots could be activated, whether the footer moved, or what happened at other zoom levels. keep the distinction between overlap and reachability; don't claim the slots were entirely unavailable or that the display was otherwise usable. the notes also mention the mobile menu, but provide no specific issue or test result for it. mark that detail as lacking a recorded finding rather than supplying one.

please ask for a memo with a brief scope statement, the provided test setup, and findings grouped by route or interaction so that someone can locate the relevant observations. for each finding, distinguish the observed behavior from any possible user effect; keep effects cautious and tied to the actual note, and don't present them as measured outcomes. identify whether a note is from NVDA, VoiceOver, or unspecified when that is recorded. where a result is missing, state that it wasn't recorded instead of treating it as a pass or failure. don't assign severity levels, compliance status, or a numeric score because no rating method or complete test record was supplied. don't add standards references, recommendations, fixes, or claims of conformance that aren't in these notes.

keep the memo readable for the library's web team, in plain professional English, with concise headings and enough detail to preserve the distinctions above. include a numbered section if it helps organize the findings, but do not force numbering where it would make the memo less clear. retain the exact quoted wording and the interface labels in quotation marks. finish with a separate short section listing the limits of the supplied evidence, including the unrecorded week date, absent full script and recordings, and mobile-menu details without a finding. the memo should report only this fictional review material; it should not claim to have tested anything itself or close with an invented approval or recommendation.", "output": "Create an internal screen-reader audit memo for Idris, not Mina, about the fictional Harborline Library consortium’s Roomline site. The site lets people search for bookable meeting rooms and make reservations. Keep the audit limited to the catalog search route and the room reservation route, including date and time selection. Do not present it as a public statement or as an audit of the entire library service.

Use only the supplied review material below. Organize it into a useful memo without implying that additional testing took place.

**Test setup and evidence**

The supplied setup was Windows 11 with Firefox 134 and NVDA 2024.4, and an iPhone SE (third generation) with iOS 18.2, Safari, and VoiceOver. Two staff members tried the routes during the same week. The notes do not give the week’s date, identify the staff members, include recordings, or provide a full test script. They also do not establish that every step was repeated with both setups. Report only what is recorded; do not invent dates, tester names, settings, or a test count beyond the two staff members.

**Findings**

1. **Catalog search.** The main heading is “Search rooms.” The search box has the accessible name “Find a room,” and the date field is marked required. After a search, the page shows a results heading and a list of available rooms. In the Windows/NVDA notes, activating the filters control opened the filter options, but the changed expanded state was not announced. The notes do not say whether the same behavior occurred with VoiceOver, or list the filter choices. Preserve the distinction between the observed behavior and any possible user effect. If using this staff quote, retain its exact wording: “I could tell the filters had opened because the page changed, but I didn't hear the button say expanded.” Do not present the staff member’s impression as a universal result.

2. **Room selection and reservation.** The recorded steps are to select a date, choose a room, choose a half-hour time slot, and submit the reservation. The notes describe a progress indicator showing the steps in order. On desktop, heading navigation moved from an H1 to an H3 in the room details area; the notes do not name an H2 or establish that one was intentionally absent. In the NVDA notes, the room-selection dialog’s close control was announced as “×.” Its accessible name on the phone was not recorded. Do not change that observation to a claim that the control had no name, and do not propose a replacement name.

   In the recorded error case, a person submitted without choosing a time slot. An error message appeared below the time selector, focus remained on the Save button, and the NVDA tester did not hear an announcement when the error appeared. The message’s exact wording and the VoiceOver result for this case were not recorded. Report the focus behavior and missing announcement separately. Do not invent the message, assume it was visually hidden, or say the issue was fixed.

   In a successful desktop test, a confirmation panel appeared after submission. Do not invent a reservation name or time, or imply that cancellation, email notices, or later booking changes were tested.

3. **Mobile time slots and menu.** At 200 percent enlargement, the sticky footer overlapped the last two time slots. VoiceOver swipe navigation could still reach both slots. The notes do not say whether both slots could be activated, whether the footer moved, or what happened at other zoom levels. Preserve the distinction between overlap and reachability; do not claim the slots were entirely unavailable or that the display was otherwise usable. The mobile menu is mentioned without a specific issue or test result. State that no finding was recorded for it rather than supplying one.

For each finding, separate observed behavior from any possible user effect. Keep possible effects cautious and tied to the notes; do not present them as measured outcomes. Identify whether a note is from NVDA, VoiceOver, or an unspecified source when the notes say. Where a result is missing, state that it was not recorded rather than treating it as a pass or failure. Do not assign severity, compliance status, or a numeric score: no rating method or complete test record was supplied. Do not add standards references, fixes, recommendations, or claims of conformance.

Write in plain professional English for the library’s web team, using concise headings and enough detail to preserve the distinctions above. Use a numbered section if it helps organize the findings, but do not force numbering where it reduces clarity. Retain the exact quoted wording and interface labels in quotation marks.

End with a short, separate section listing the limits of the supplied evidence: the week’s date is unrecorded, the full script and recordings are absent, and the mobile-menu mention has no specific finding. Report only this fictional review material. Do not claim to have performed tests, and do not close with an invented approval or recommendation."}]
